subject: SLA exception & remedy terms for MediCore pilot
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SLA variance for MediCore pilot

Hi Lauren —

Quick one: MediCore (healthcare SaaS) is asking for a commercial variance on our standard SLA for a 3-month pilot they want to run starting Sept 1. Their asks are: 

- Temporary uptime target: 99.5% (vs our standard 99.9%) for the pilot period
- Service credit cap reduced (they want no credits until remediation, but they proposed a 2% cap)
- 20% committed-capacity discount if they commit to 12 months after pilot

They've attached a short request doc (MediCore_MA-Request-2026-08-11.pdf). Deal basics: expected ARR if converted ~ $1.2M, deal_id DEAL-9876.

From a risk perspective, they are highly regulated and will push on uptime language. Sales asks: can we offer a provisional 99.5% pilot SLA with a commercial remedy that limits downside (so we don't set an open precedent), and a discount to close? Need deal-desk + exec sign-off because this changes remedy caps and pricing.

Can you greenlight escalation to Deal Desk and Legal? We need a decision this week to keep their procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Rishi
--
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SLA variance for MediCore pilot

Thanks Rishi — forwarding to Deal Desk (Vivek) and looping Marissa & Neha.

Two quick clarifying asks before we formalize: 
1) What exact remedy thresholds are they expecting (e.g., credit at <99.5% OR staged credits)?
2) If we offer a 20% committed discount after conversion, can you confirm ARR assumptions and timing (12-month commit start date)?

Also attach any HA / onboarding runbook or architecture notes from the SRE pilot plan — Legal will need that to scope carveouts. I don't want to approve anything that removes our basic availability protections; provisional variance can be allowed if we cap financial exposure and require an SRE support add-on.

If you can drop a one-pager with the exact wording they want in redlines (or highlight in the attached draft SLA), I'll route for a fast exec review.

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 08:26:00 -0700
Subject: Deal Desk analysis & recommended guardrails for MediCore SLA exception

Team — I reviewed the ask and ran financial exposure scenarios. Summary and recommendation: 

Summary of the request:
- Pilot period: 3 months (Sept–Nov)
- Temporary SLA target: 99.5%
- Customer requested removal of standard service credit triggers; wants minimal credits
- Commercial ask: 20% committed discount on 12-month post-pilot commitment

Deal Desk recommended configuration (to balance risk & commercial):
- Approve a provisional SLA of 99.5% for a maximum 6-month period (we can't allow an indefinite permanent roll).
- Service credit structure: staged credits starting only below 99.0% during pilot; cap total credits at 5% of monthly invoice (company-wide cap) — this is less than their ask but protects us vs open liability.
- Require SRE onboarding add-on for the pilot (one-time fee or cost-pass-through) and a documented runbook + monthly QA checkpoints.
- Approve a 15% committed-capacity discount (12-month commitment) instead of 20%. Offer the additional 5% as a Q3 commercial incentive (contract amendment) contingent on meeting performance goals in month 1.
- Legal to add explicit carveouts for force majeure, customer-side misconfigurations, and scheduled maintenance windows.

Risks / precedent: this creates a template that other regulated customers will request. If Execs sign off, we should save the approval as a precedent with strict metadata (region, account size, duration).

Attachments: deal_analysis_medicore.xlsx (workbook with exposure models). HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/9876

If Lauren/Marissa support, request exec sign-off (Stephanie or Lauren can approve at director level; anything beyond a 6-month variance should go to the VP).

- Vivek
--
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Deal Desk, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 14:41:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Deal Desk analysis & recommended guardrails for MediCore SLA exception

Lauren / Vivek — I support Vivek's recommended guardrails. A few commercial notes: 
- MediCore is strategic for our healthcare vertical; they have strong references and will likely expand to 3 additional products if the pilot succeeds.
- Expected ARR on conversion: ~$1.2M; short term: they sign the pilot PO quickly if we move on the SLA ask.

Recommendation: Approve the proposed variance (6-month max, 99.5% pilot SLA, 5% credit cap, 15% committed discount) so we can lock the PO and move to SRE onboarding. If Lauren wants, escalate to Stephanie for a final opt-in but we need the decision by Friday to keep procurement on track.

Forwarding full thread.

Marissa

VP, Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: APPROVED: MediCore provisional SLA & associated commercial terms

Team — after reviewing the analysis and talking briefly with Finance, I approve the following, to be captured in the SLA amendment and contract: 

1) Provisional pilot SLA: 99.5% uptime for a maximum of 6 months (pilot may be shorter).
2) Service credit policy during pilot: credits only trigger if monthly availability < 99.0%; total credit liability capped at 5% of that month's invoice.
3) Required SRE onboarding + runbook to be completed before pilot start; SRE add-on to be billed separately or cost-offset from onboarding budget.
4) Committed discount: 15% for a 12-month post-pilot commitment. Additional commercial incentives (up to 5% more) can be applied as a separate promotional amendment contingent on month-1 performance.
5) Legal to include clear carveouts (scheduled maintenance windows, customer misconfiguration, force majeure).

Next steps:
- Rishi: confirm the customer's acceptance of the above with Elena (evargas@medicore.com) and get signed PO for the pilot.
- Neha: prepare onboarding plan with SREs and share runbook template.
- Vivek/Legal: update SLA amendment draft (SLA_Amendment_Draft.docx) and prepare DocuSign envelope.

I'm copying Stephanie for visibility; if anything materially changes (longer variance, higher credit exposure), escalate to VP approval.

Lauren
